abstracts.abstract: This paper proposes a novel distributed cognitive multi-agent control paradigm for complex industrial process automation that fundamentally reconceptualizes the interaction between knowledge representation and dynamic control execution. Unlike conventional centralized AI control architectures, the proposed framework introduces hierarchical cognitive agents where each agent maintains local knowledge bases and engages in peer-to-peer reasoning to achieve emergent global control objectives. The paradigm integrates fuzzy logic for imprecise sensor data interpretation, neural networks for adaptive pattern recognition, and evolutionary computation for on-line parameter optimization within a unified multi-agent architecture. We formalize the cognitive interaction protocols using graph-theoretic models and prove convergence properties under bounded disturbance conditions. Extensive simulation experiments on benchmark chemical process control problems demonstrate that the proposed paradigm achieves superior tracking performance and fault tolerance compared to state-of-the-art centralized and decentralized control methods. The framework naturally supports heterogeneous agent capabilities and scalable deployment in large-scale industrial systems. This work establishes a new research direction that bridges knowledge-based systems, distributed AI, and intelligent control, offering a paradigm shift for AI applications in manufacturing and industrial automation where robustness and adaptability are critical.

This paper presents a significant improvement to deep reinforcement learning algorithms for intelligent fault diagnosis in rotating machinery within industrial automation contexts. While existing DRL approaches have shown promise for sequential fault detection, they suffer from poor sample efficiency and unreliable convergence when handling high-dimensional sensory data from complex mechanical systems. We propose a novel uncertainty-aware deep Q-network architecture that incorporates Bayesian neural networks for robust action selection and epistemic uncertainty quantification. The improved method introduces a prioritized experience replay mechanism specifically designed for imbalanced fault datasets commonly encountered in real engineering applications. Furthermore, we develop a multi-scale feature attention module that extracts discriminative representations from vibration signals at multiple temporal resolutions. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets and a real-world turbocharged compressor fault diagnosis task demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves 15.3% higher diagnostic accuracy while reducing training sample requirements by 40% compared to conventional deep reinforcement learning methods. The uncertainty quantification mechanism also provides reliable confidence estimates for diagnostic decisions, which is essential for safety-critical AI applications in aerospace and industrial environments. This work advances the state-of-the-art in machine learning for fault diagnosis and provides practical guidelines for deploying DRL-based diagnostic systems in real engineering contexts.

This paper presents a novel end-to-end learning-based visual servoing system for industrial robotic manipulation that fundamentally changes the integration paradigm between computer vision and robot control. Traditional approaches treat visual perception and motion control as separate modules connected through hand-designed interfaces, which limits system adaptability and real-time performance. The proposed architecture employs a hierarchical neural network structure where low-level visual features are directly mapped to motor commands through learnable attention mechanisms, eliminating the need for explicit camera calibration or precise geometric modeling. The system incorporates evolutionary computation for automatically optimizing the neural controller parameters in simulation, followed by rapid fine-tuning on physical robots using minimal real-world samples. We design a distributed computing framework that achieves real-time performance at 60Hz on standard industrial computing hardware. The complete system was deployed on a 6-DOF robotic arm for precision assembly tasks in an AI manufacturing environment. Experimental results demonstrate successful manipulation of previously unseen objects with sub-millimeter positioning accuracy, outperforming conventional model-based visual servoing approaches. The proposed paradigm enables rapid deployment of intelligent robotic systems without extensive manual engineering, representing a significant advancement in AI applications for industrial robotics and automated manufacturing.

This paper presents a significantly improved intelligent energy management system for industrial facilities that integrates advanced neural network forecasting with evolutionary optimization algorithms for real-time operational decision-making. Existing industrial energy management approaches typically employ simplified prediction models and static optimization rules, which fail to capture the complex nonlinear dynamics of energy consumption patterns in modern manufacturing environments. The proposed system incorporates a hybrid forecasting module combining long short-term memory networks with attention mechanisms for accurate prediction of electricity demand and renewable energy generation. For optimization, we develop an enhanced multi-objective evolutionary algorithm with adaptive operator selection and covariance matrix adaptation that significantly improves convergence speed and solution quality compared to standard evolutionary methods. The complete system architecture includes an edge computing layer for real-time data processing and a cloud-based optimization engine for strategic planning. Extensive validation was conducted over a six-month period across three industrial plants, demonstrating 18.7% reduction in energy costs and 23.4% improvement in renewable energy utilization compared to existing commercial energy management solutions. The system provides interpretable decision support through knowledge-based explanations of optimization recommendations. This work delivers a practical and significantly enhanced solution for AI in energy applications, with direct implications for sustainable manufacturing operations and carbon footprint reduction in industrial sectors.
